set.pl: NW corner of sec 16, Clay Twp (T74N R9W), Washington Co (Burrell 1909, Clay chapter); alternative reading Iowa Twp sec 16
pinev: Burrell 1909, Clay chapter: he 'sold his place in Clay' and on the gallows said he had buried $5,000 'at the foot of a red oak tree in the northwest corner of section 16 in Iowa'. No period paper yet.

Burrell's 1844 township list gives Iowa as T76-77N R6W; Highland (T77N R6W) was split off in 1854. Two readings: 'in Iowa' as the state puts the oak in Clay Twp, the chapter the story is told in; as Iowa Twp (T76N R6W after 1854, T77N R6W before) it lies 20 mi NE. Primary pin Clay: sec 16 T74N R9W from BLM PLSS (box 41.2061-41.2211 / -91.9071 to -91.8876), pin just inside the NW corner.
1906 Washington Co atlas, Clay Twp (Ancestry image 31617_072148-00043): the NW of sec 16 is cut into small Morgan family lots (C. B. Morgan and others), so the corner was built up by 1906.

set.n: Nicholas Koster, miser, house burned near Sac Bay, Delta Co
pinev: 1900 census (Sack Bay Twp) lists him between households that the 1913 Delta atlas and patrons list place in secs 19 and 21 T38N R19W; his 1909 death record is Fairbanks Twp, which includes Sac Bay. No Koster tract on the 1913 atlas (he died 1909); the ring covers secs 19-22 (BLM PLSS). The 1909 Detroit News said only 'Garden', the nearest village.
1900 census: Nicklos Coster, 73, b. Germany, Sac Bay, Delta Co, the only candidate for the miser.
